title: Practice: Safe DOM Manipulation
prompt: Audit a widget for safe dom manipulation. Test keyboard operation, visible feedback, safe text rendering, and its server-side trust boundary.
objective: Apply safe dom manipulation in a controlled example and demonstrate expected behavior with a small test.
target_skills: The difference between text and HTML insertion
expected_output: The untrusted message is inserted as text, not parsed as HTML.

public_tests.name: Human review
checklist: Behavior matches the prompt and documented expected result.
At least one relevant edge case is checked.
Keyboard and accessibility behavior is verified where relevant.
The learner can explain one implementation choice and one limitation.

acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate the core behavior for safe dom manipulation.
Include a repeatable check or written evidence for expected output.
Handle an empty, repeated, malformed, or failure state where it applies.
Keep user-provided content safe and describe any server-side responsibility.
hints: Break safe dom manipulation into the smallest requirements.
Use the narrowest selector or API that expresses the task clearly.
Inspect the browser console and the changed DOM/request before changing more code.
grading_method: Server-side required-string smoke check plus rubric/human review; this check does not prove runtime correctness, accessibility, or production readiness.
retry_policy: Retries are allowed. Incorrect or incomplete answers do not complete the exercise or award XP; the platform applies its fixed idempotent exercise reward only after a verified correct completion.
